title: Rotation-consensus decode: confidence = agreement across four headings, baked into the exported graph
hypothesis: Prignitz's entire gap to Berlin is false fixes (3.75% vs 0.50%; usable, abstention and median error barely move). The mechanism CLAUDE.md diagnoses is belief mass landing confidently on ONE wrong field that looks like the right one -- a case single-view pooled-mass confidence cannot see, because a wrong unimodal peak is indistinguishable from a right one. But training draws a fresh uniform-random heading per position per epoch, so a genuinely memorized place is heading-invariant by construction, while a false match to a look-alike twin rides view-specific micro-texture cues that should not survive rotating the same frame. Requiring cross-heading consensus therefore separates the two cases: right answers keep their pooled mass, heading-dependent wrong answers split their mass across distant blocks and drop below the frozen 0.3 confidence threshold, converting false fixes into abstentions at zero training cost. If instead usable_fix_rate collapses, we learn the aliasing is rotation-stable -- equally decisive, and it would redirect the era toward training-time disambiguation.
method: Change ONLY CellLocNet.forward() in model/model.py (the deployed decode). Build a 4-view batch from the input -- the frame plus its 90/180/270-degree rotations (via transpose+flip so the ONNX export uses only Transpose/Slice ops) -- run the existing shared trunk once over that batch, softmax each view's cell logits, average the four belief distributions, and run the existing 3x3 pooled decode (argmax -> neighborhood mask -> mass-weighted centroid -> conf) on the AVERAGED belief. The within-cell offset nudge comes from the unrotated view only. training_outputs(), loss_fn, targets and train.py are untouched: this is a test-time consensus mechanism living entirely inside the exported graph.
expected_outcome: Baseline: mission 0.112653, usable 92.5%, false 3.75% (15/400), abstain 3.75%, coverage 96.25%. A false fix on the averaged belief now needs the same wrong 3x3 block to win in at least ~2 of 4 headings, so predict false_fix_rate drops to <=1.5% (<=6/400) with usable_fix_rate within about one point of 92.5% (the 4-view ensemble average may even add correct fixes) -> mission_score <= 0.09, plausibly ~0.07. Failure modes that would refute it: usable drops >3 points (rotation-stable aliasing / consensus too strict for the 0.3 threshold), or false fixes barely move (the wrong twins fool all headings). Coverage stays far above the 0.2 FAIL floor. Gates: ~3.1 MB ONNX unchanged (weights shared across the 4-view batch), latency ~4x of 1.58 ms host proxy, versus a 250 ms gate.
eli5: The model sometimes lands confidently on the wrong farm field because, from one angle, it looks identical to the right one. So before trusting an answer, we now show the model the same photo four times, turned 90 degrees each time -- like double-checking a guess by looking at the map from four directions. A place it truly knows gets the same answer every time; a lucky look-alike match changes its answer when the picture turns. When the four answers disagree, the model now says 'I don't know' instead of feeding a wrong position to the aircraft -- and for this aircraft, a wrong answer is far more dangerous than no answer.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128×128 px daytime crop, Prignitz only, no synthetic lighting variants

stages.name: Four-heading views
stages.detail: the same frame plus copies turned 90°, 180° and 270° -- four looks at the identical ground

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: small from-scratch conv trunk (4 stride-2 blocks) shared across all four views, summarizing each into one feature vector

stages.name: Cell belief map
stages.detail: each view votes a probability over the ~3,000 map cells (128 m squares) plus a within-cell nudge

stages.name: Consensus pooled decode
stages.detail: the four views' beliefs are averaged before the usual 3×3 neighborhood pooling; only ground all four headings agree on keeps high confidence

stages.name: Fix + confidence
stages.detail: mass-weighted centroid of the agreed neighborhood plus the unrotated view's nudge → (lat, lon, confidence); disagreement falls below the 0.3 threshold and abstains

implementation_brief: Edit model/model.py ONLY; model/train.py is untouched. (1) In CellLocNet, add a private helper for exact 90-degree rotation that avoids torch.rot90 (unreliable in the legacy ONNX exporter): rot90 CCW of x[B,C,H,W] is x.transpose(2,3).flip(2); apply it 1, 2, and 3 times for 90/180/270. Input is square (128x128) so these are exact, interpolation-free, and export as Transpose/Slice ops under opset 17, dynamo=False. (2) Rewrite forward(x) as: B = x.shape[0]; x4 = torch.cat([x, r90(x), r180(x), r270(x)], dim=0)  # [4B,3,128,128], trunk weights shared, stored once in the ONNX; logits, offset = self.training_outputs(x4); p = F.softmax(logits, dim=1).reshape(4, B, n_cells).mean(dim=0)  # averaged belief, rows still sum to 1; offset = offset[:B]  # unrotated view's nudge only -- do NOT try to de-rotate/average the other three (sign conventions are not worth the risk and the nudge is a sub-cell refinement). Then run the EXISTING decode verbatim on p instead of a fresh softmax: idx = p.argmax(dim=1); same 1.6-pitch Chebyshev 3x3 mask; q = p * mask; conf = q.sum(dim=1); mass-weighted centroid; add offset[:,0]*scale_u / offset[:,1]*scale_v; clamp; return torch.stack([u, v, conf], dim=1). conf remains a sub-sum of an averaged softmax so it stays in [0,1]. Keep the reshape order consistent with the cat order (view k occupies rows k*B:(k+1)*B). forward() must keep working for any batch size B, not just 1. (3) training_outputs(), loss_fn(), make_soft_targets/residual_offset_target in train.py, __init__ buffers, grid geometry, CELL_PX and export_onnx() all stay byte-identical. Accepted known mismatch, do not 'fix' it: train.py's residual_offset_target mirrors the OLD single-view pooling; that stays as-is (both centroids coincide when views agree, and when they disagree conf is low and the frame abstains anyway). (4) Contracts to preserve: train.py CLI (--area --out-dir --data-dir --epochs --max-crops-per-bucket --seed) unchanged; export contract per model/model.py docstring -- one ONNX per area at <out>/models/<area>.onnx, input 1x3x128x128 float32 in [0,1], output [[u, v, conf]] with u,v normalized map coords, conf in [0,1]; opset 17, dynamo=False. (5) Update model/model.py's module docstring and forward()'s comment to describe the rotation-consensus decode. (6) Sanity check before finishing: export a dummy-meta model to ONNX and run one onnxruntime inference on a 1x3x128x128 zeros input; confirm output shape [1,3], conf in [0,1], and no exporter warnings about rot90/flip fallbacks.
